messages:
elaine_sales: Quick sync — NovaHealth POC hitting intermittent generation timeouts when they run a mixed workload (TS frontend + Python backend) behind their corporate proxy. They see ~5–10% of requests fail with "upstream timeout" and occasional 502s. They want it stable for next week's exec demo. Anyone free to swarm?
ben_engineering: on it. can you paste a minimal repro logs/snippet? suspect connection reuse / keepalive mismatch between SDKs.
elaine_sales: pasted log snippet from their dev environment:
```
2025-04-11T15:12:03Z ERROR request_id=abcd1234 upstream_error="504 Gateway Timeout" route=/v1/generate client=python-sdk
2025-04-11T15:12:03Z WARN request_id=abcd1234 retry_attempt=1 reason=stream-reset
2025-04-11T15:12:04Z INFO request_id=efgh5678 ts-client idle_reuse=true
```
They also said TS client appears to succeed more often, but when both clients hit concurrently the backend Python ones time out.
priya_support: that sounds like connection pooling differences. python-requests default keepalive + proxy might be opening new connections instead of reusing. Are they using the official Redwood Python SDK or a custom wrapper? Also, do they set HTTP_PROXY/HTTPS_PROXY env vars?
ravi_sre: tagging networking stuff — also check their proxy config for connection limits. Many corp proxies have per-IP concurrent connection caps which break long-poll/stream workloads.
elaine_sales: they said: using our python sdk v0.9.3 through requests, and ts sdk v1.1.2 on node. proxy is a corporate forward proxy (SawtoothCorp) with auth token. They set env var `HTTPS_PROXY=https://proxy.sawtooth.local:8443`. NO_PROXY not set.
ben_engineering: two quick hypotheses: 1) proxy connection pooling + lack of NO_PROXY causing extra hops, 2) session affinity / cookie-based balancing in the proxy causing stickiness that interacts badly with older python requests' Connection: keep-alive under proxies. Workarounds: enable SDK-level keepalive adapter or set NO_PROXY for direct traffic to our endpoints. Also tune retries/backoff and streaming chunk timeouts.
priya_support: sample python patch to enable persistent pool and retries we recommend:
```
from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry
import requests
s = requests.Session()
retries = Retry(total=5, backoff_factor=0.4, status_forcelist=[429,502,503,504])
s.mount('https://', HTTPAdapter(pool_maxsize=100, max_retries=retries, pool_block=True))
# use s for Redwood client HTTP transport
```
ben_engineering: also add `NO_PROXY=api.redwood.ai,*.redwood.internal` (replace with actual host) so traffic to our inference edges skips their corporate proxy. That often fixes the 50x series.
elaine_sales: customer asked whether we can recommend parameters for Dedicated/reserved capacity if proxies remain flaky — they want to know cost impact and whether Dedicated avoids this.
ben_engineering: Dedicated helps if the issue is upstream capacity or noisy neighbors on our hosted pool; it won't bypass their corporate proxy. If they go Private (VPC peering or on-prem), proxy influence is eliminated. For pricing: estimate their baseline QPS and token throughput; we can run a quick model. I can draft a sizing note.
ravi_sre: small networking note — if they cannot set NO_PROXY, another option is to force HTTP/1.1 keepalive and reuse connections to the proxy by pooling aggressively from the client. Also prefer shorter idle_timeout on our side to avoid stale backend connections.
elaine_sales: they also attached a redacted security questionnaire asking if proxy-related traffic logs leave PII. SecOps question: do we log client IPs or headers that might contain user identifiers?
secops_bot: redwood infra typically logs source IP at the edge for RT-run metrics; headers are NOT stored by default except a few routing headers. For PII-sensitive workloads recommend Private deployment + KMS + audit log retention controls. I'll send a short FAQ blurb.
priya_support: action items for triage: 1) ben — draft python SDK patch + backoff sample and small troubleshooting script; 2) ravi — run quick checklist for proxy caps and session affinity; 3) secops_bot — supply the FAQ snippet and recommended config for NO_PROXY/privacy notes; 4) elaine — ask customer to run the attached reproduce script and share results by EOD.
ben_engineering: will push sample patch and a small repro script that toggles NO_PROXY and shows per-connection stats. quick snippet for node side too (agent keepalive):
```
const agent = new https.Agent({ keepAlive: true, maxSockets: 50 });
const client = new RedwoodClient({ transport: { agent } });
```
priya_support: Also call out retry jitter and respect for 429. If they hammer with sync retries without jitter, proxy queues blow up. In the python snippet above the Retry config handles 429 gracefully.
elaine_sales: thanks — I'll coordinate demo timeline. If we can get a quick test run tomorrow morning, I'll consolidate for the exec.
deploybot: deploy check: no infra changes required for these client-side mitigations.
ben_engineering: one more obs — if they see stream resets, set shorter chunk timeout on client and enable reconnect with resumed KV cache where possible (reduces full-run cost). I'll include pointers.
elaine_sales: perfect. tagging @novah-cto to request NO_PROXY test and their proxy logs. :thumbsup:
priya_support: standing by for results, happy to jump on call with customer. :phone:
secops_bot: sending FAQ + redacted log policy now (private link)
elaine_sales: closing loop here once tests run — will post results in this thread. Thanks team!
